html:
Pratap Singh was ruler of Mewar in southern Rajasthan from 1572 to 1597. He is remembered as the Rajput king who never submitted to Akbar.

By the 1570s most Rajput houses had made peace with the Mughals, given daughters in marriage and taken high rank in the imperial army. Mewar, the senior house, had not. Akbar had stormed its fortress of Chittor in 1568, in the reign of Pratap's father, who then founded Udaipur. Pratap turned away four embassies.

On 18 June 1576 a Mughal army under Man Singh of Amber, himself a Rajput, met Pratap at the pass of Haldighati. Pratap had about 3,000 horsemen and some Bhil archers against a force several times larger. After a few hours he was wounded and his men were driven from the field. Legend says his horse Chetak carried him to safety and then died.

Akbar's troops took the towns but could not catch him. He fought on from the hills for twenty years, living rough, and after 1582 won back most of western Mewar. He never retook Chittor. He died in 1597; his son made peace with the Mughals in 1615.

In modern India he is a hero of resistance, with statues in many cities.
